results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
**Mono-green storm for Premodern: Hunting Pack off a pile of cheap spells and mana elves (brew, borrowing mana and sideboard ideas from the Elves archetype)**

**Plan.** Play mana creatures and free or cheap spells (Lotus Petal, Land Grant, Vitalize, Emerald Charm). Rofellos and the elves give you 7 mana. Then cast Hunting Pack, which is the only green storm payoff in the pool. Every spell cast before it that turn adds a copy and a 4/4 Beast, and creature spells count. At storm 4–6, cast it at the end of the opponent's turn to get 5–7 Beasts. They are summoning sick when they arrive, so they attack the turn after.

**Changes from the submitted 60.** The engine (Pack, Vines, Land Grant, Petal, Vitalize, Charm, Rofellos, both elves) is untouched.
- **Untappers.** The deck had 14 untap effects, which is too many. I cut Wirewood Symbiote from 3 copies to 1 and added 2 Birds of Paradise. Birds is a one-mana mana source that also counts as a spell. Birds is on Elves reference lists, but I didn't measure its effect here.
- **Gaea's Cradle.** One Cradle replaces one Forest, so the deck runs 16 Forests, 1 Cradle and 17 lands. The deck has about 19 creatures before Pack tokens. Elves lists play about 3.7 Cradles. I kept 16 Forests so Rofellos, Land Grant and Nature's Lore still have enough targets.
- **Sideboard.** I cut Multani's Acolyte and a Tormod's Crypt. In their place: a second Ravenous Baloth and a second Wall of Blossoms.

**Mana, from the simulator (5,000 games).**
- The mulligan rate is 9.6%.
- Colour problems are 0%.
- Pack is in hand by turn 4 in 16.2% of games, up from 13.7% before my changes. Some of that gain may come from the extra mana creatures rather than from Pack itself.
- The simulator reports a 37.4% "screw rate". It models only land drops, not elves, Petal, Land Grant or Rofellos, so it overstates how mana-starved the deck is.
- It also reports 0% "engine ready by turn 4". It can't model a 7-mana storm turn, so I have no measured number for how often the combo goes off.
- The deck check gives an average mana value of 1.86. It recommends 18.7 lands. I judge the elves, Birds, Lore and Grant make up the difference, but that is unmeasured.

**Matchups (meta shares from the last 30 days).**
- **Enchantress (12.5%).** Favourable on speed. Bring in Naturalize and Xantid Swarm.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%).** Creatures survive, but Rofellos and Pack's 7 mana do not. Bring in Walls and Naturalize.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%).** Naturalize hits Dreadnought. Xantid Swarm stops spells, which helps against their counters and Stifle.
- **Sligh (9.9%) and Goblins (4.4%).** These are the worst matchups, because they kill the mana creatures. Bring in Masticore ×2, Ravenous Baloth ×2 and the Wall of Blossoms copies. Baloth can sacrifice a Beast token to gain 4 life.
- **Hermit Druid Combo (5.5%).** It wins first. Xantid Swarm is the only real answer in the sideboard.
- **Replenish and UB Psychatog (4.8% each).** Tormod's Crypt is the only graveyard hate, so keep it for Replenish. Xantid Swarm is the plan against Psychatog's counters.

**Unverified.**
- The matchup advice is judgment, not measured.
- Pack is one big spell with no protection, so counterspells and Stifle effects can stop the whole turn.
- I did not check how often each opponent has removal for the elves.

intent.goal: Build a mono green deck in Premodern that functions as a storm deck, chaining spells together for a storm-count payoff using only green cards.

engine.thesis: Mono green has one real storm payoff in Premodern, Hunting Pack (Scourge, 7 mana instant, makes a 4/4 Beast per copy), so the deck ramps with Rofellos and mana elves. It then chains free and cheap spells (Land Grant, Lotus Petal, Sprouting Vines) and untap effects (Vitalize, Emerald Charm) to build storm and cast Pack for several 4/4s. Premodern is the only format here with the storm cards and with Rofellos, Land Grant and Lotus Petal together.
engine.winCondition: Cast Hunting Pack with storm 4-6, ideally at the end of the opponent's turn, to make 5-7 4/4 Beasts, then attack the next turn. The tokens are summoning sick when they come in, so the win comes a turn later.
beats: Slower durdle decks such as Standstill and Enchantress
Creature-light decks that cannot race a wide board of 4/4s
losesTo: Sligh and Goblins (fast red aggro, and removal on the mana creatures)
Terrageddon and Stiflenought (they destroy lands or race, and the deck folds if the elves and Rofellos are removed)
Counterspells and Stifle effects (Hunting Pack is one big spell with no protection)

results.prompt: Give me a stock Goblins list for Premodern.
results.text:
**Mono-red Goblins (stock)** is the most recent top Goblins list from the Premodern results, a 5-0 league run dated 2026-10-14. I submitted it unchanged and it passed check_deck. In the last 30 days Goblins was 4.4% of the field (34 lists, measured).

**Plan:** Start with Goblin Lackey, Mogg Fanatic or Goblin Piledriver, then add Goblin Warchief and Goblin Ringleader. Goblin Matron fetches whichever Goblin the board needs. Finish with burn from Gempalm Incinerator, Siege-Gang Commander and Mogg Fanatic.

**Key cards:**
- **Goblin Lackey and Goblin Piledriver:** these are the fast starts.
- **Goblin Warchief:** it makes Goblins cheaper and gives them haste.
- **Goblin Matron and Goblin Ringleader:** these keep the hand full and find the right Goblin.
- **Goblin Sharpshooter, Goblin Tinkerer and Skirk Prospector:** these are one-of utility cards.
- **Rishadan Port and Wasteland:** these slow down or cut off opposing mana. I read that role from the card names and common play, not from a tool result.

**Mana (24 lands):** 17 Mountain, 4 Rishadan Port and 3 Wasteland. In check_deck that gives 17.5 red sources, against a real-Goblins average of about 17.0. The land count of 24 matches the recommended 23.9 and the Goblins average of 23.97. In 5,000 simulated games:

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 15.1% |
| Screw rate | 6.9% |
| Flood rate | 3.7% |
| Red mana available on turn 3 | 91.7% |
| Early drop in hand by turn 3 | 86.9% |
| Early drop castable by turn 3 | 84.8% |

The early drops here are Lackey, Fanatic, Piledriver and Prospector. The simulation only models land drops and colored mana, not card abilities.

**Sideboard:** I haven't tested these matchups, so the plans below are judgment from the card names and the field.
- **Sligh and other fast red decks:** bring in 3 Pyrokinesis and 3 Red Elemental Blast.
- **Enchantress, Standstill, and other decks that want to stall the game:** bring in 2 Anarchy to destroy white permanents. Keep the pressure on.
- **Hermit Druid Combo and Replenish:** bring in 3 Tormod's Crypt, which exiles graveyards.
- **Stiflenought and UB Psychatog (blue decks):** bring in Red Elemental Blast.
- **Terrageddon:** the sideboard has no specific answer to Terrageddon. Wasteland and Rishadan Port are the main game plan against it.
- **Overload, Mogg Salvage and the extra Goblin Goon** are the remaining sideboard slots. Overload and Mogg Salvage are artifact answers.

**Unverified:** I didn't re-read every card's text with card_info. The role descriptions come from the list and the tool outputs I saw.

intent.goal: Deliver a proven, established Goblins decklist for the Premodern format.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
**Mono-white Replenish with no blue (brew, borrowing the mana base and the Replenish/Opalescence/Parallax Wave core from the tournament Replenish lists)**

**Plan.** The fastest line is Lion's Eye Diamond. Cast Replenish with Ancient Tomb or Mox Diamond plus LED, so your hand of Opalescence, Parallax Wave, Worship and Solitary Confinement is discarded as you cast it. Replenish then returns all of them. Opalescence turns the enchantments into creatures, Parallax Wave exiles blockers, and Worship and Solitary Confinement keep you alive. Tireless Tribe is a one-mana discard outlet for slower games, and Enlightened Tutor finds LED, Opalescence or a Mox.

**What I changed in the review**
- **Land count.** I cut one Swords to Plowshares for a 15th Plains, which takes the deck from 21 to 22 lands. In the simulation of the submitted 21-land list, 21.8% of games were land-screwed and the average was 3.22 lands in play on turn 4. With 22 lands, screw fell to 10.5% and the average rose to 3.51. The mulligan rate also rose, from 8.7% to 19.3%. I can't explain that jump, so treat that comparison cautiously.
- **Sideboard.** Unchanged.

**Why the key cards**
- **Ancient Tomb, Mox Diamond, LED.** Tomb gives two mana and LED gives three. Tomb plus LED alone is five mana, enough for Replenish on turn 1. This is my own mana count, not a simulation. The simulator doesn't model card abilities, so its "engine ready" figure was 0% and tells you nothing here.
- **Draw odds.** By turn 2 on the play (8 cards seen), you have Replenish, LED and a Tomb or Mox together 9.1% of the time. If you count Enlightened Tutor as a second Replenish, a fourth LED and a Tomb or Mox, it is 19.1%. The fourth LED isn't in the deck. So expect the turn-1 kill occasionally and a slower, grindier game most of the time.
- **Swords to Plowshares and Abeyance.** Swords answers Stiflenought's big creatures and Sligh's and Terrageddon's attackers. Abeyance stops the opponent casting instants or sorceries and activating abilities that turn. Cast it before Replenish, it protects against counterspells and Tormod's Crypt, which 97.8% of Enchantress sideboards play.
- **Cards that are dead when LED discards your hand.** Swords and Abeyance are the cost of that interaction, since neither is an enchantment.

**Matchups (judgment from the tournament data)**

| Matchup | Share of field | How it goes | Sideboard plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enchantress | 12.5% | Their key creatures have shroud, so Swords is weak against them. | Take out 2 Swords. Bring in 2 Aura of Silence and 1–2 Orim's Chant. Hold Seal of Cleansing for artifacts and enchantments that matter. |
| Terrageddon | 11.2% | Mox Diamond, Moxen and Ancient Tomb help us rebuild after Armageddon. | Bring in Wrath of God and kicked Orim's Chant. Swords stays in. |
| Stiflenought | 10.4% | The hardest matchup. Stifle and counterspells can stop Replenish, so Abeyance matters. | Bring in the 2 extra Abeyance and 2 Defense Grid. Keep Swords for Dreadnought. |
| Sligh | 9.9% | Ancient Tomb's 2 damage hurts. Solitary Confinement and Worship help. | Bring in 3 Exalted Angel and Sphere of Law. Take out Seal of Cleansing and the Tribes if needed. |
| Hermit Druid | 5.5% | Faster than us. | No specific plan. |

**Unverified**
- I couldn't test the deck against opposing lists, so the matchup notes above are reasoning.
- You can still lose to graveyard hate, enchantment removal on Opalescence, and discard.
- Solitary Confinement will usually be sacrificed on your first upkeep after a Replenish, because the hand is empty. It protects you for one turn cycle.
- I didn't change the engine. The Rune of Protection cycling enchantments (e.g. Rune of Protection: Red) could fill the graveyard and cycle, but I didn't test them.

intent.goal: Deliver a Premodern Replenish-style deck (reanimating enchantments/creatures en masse from the graveyard) built without any blue cards.

engine.thesis: Mono-white-based Replenish with no blue: since Attunement and Careful Study are out, the deck fills its graveyard with Lion's Eye Diamond (discard the whole hand while Replenish is being cast), Tireless Tribe, Solitary Confinement and self-sacrificing enchantments like Seal of Cleansing and Parallax Wave. Replenish then returns Opalescence, Parallax Wave and Worship together, so the enchantments become 4/4 creatures that are protected by the Wave and Worship. The aim is to do this by turn 1-4, using Mox Diamond and Enlightened Tutor to speed it up and to fetch pieces.
engine.winCondition: Replenish returns Opalescence plus Parallax Wave, Worship and other enchantments from the graveyard. They become creatures that attack the next turn, while Parallax Wave exiles blockers and Worship and Solitary Confinement keep us alive.
beats: Enchantress (it is slower and the Wave can exile its blockers)
Sligh (Solitary Confinement and Worship stop damage)
Control decks with few ways to attack the graveyard
losesTo: Counterspells, Duress/Therapy effects and Wasteland on key pieces
Enchantment removal (Seal of Cleansing, Abolish, Disenchant) used on Opalescence
Stiflenought and fast Hermit Druid combo

results.prompt: Build a Modern deck around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
Tainted Pact isn't legal in Modern, so the classic Thassa's Oracle + Tainted Pact combo can't be built. Oracle is legal. Demonic Consultation is also not legal, and Doomsday isn't either. Spoils of the Vault is legal but costs 1 life per exiled card, so it doesn't work as a stand-in for Pact. I built the nearest working deck: an Oracle deck that wins by emptying its own library, using the Song of Creation list from recent Modern results.

**Plan.** Get Song of Creation out and draw two cards for every spell you cast. Chain the free artifacts and cheap spells (Mishra's Bauble, the Moxen, Repeal, Boomerang Basics). Win with Thassa's Oracle or Jace, Wielder of Mysteries once the library is nearly or fully empty, or with Grapeshot as a backup. Oracle is a 2-of here, and the Song list I borrowed from ran Oracle in only 15.6% of lists (a measured figure).

**Key cards**
- **Song of Creation (4):** It draws the library for you. It also makes you discard your hand each end step, so you need to win that turn.
- **Thassa's Oracle (2):** It's the closest remaining piece of your request. Its win condition needs devotion to blue at least equal to the cards left in your library. Jace (UUU), Emry, Tamiyo and Song itself add to devotion.
- **Jace, Wielder of Mysteries (1):** It wins when you draw from an empty library. That gives a second way to win that doesn't depend on devotion.
- **Mishra's Bauble, Mox Amber, Mox Opal, Emry:** They are the free spells and mana that let you cast many spells in one turn.
- **Malevolent Rumble and Preordain:** They dig for pieces. These are my substitute for Pact's card selection, and they are much weaker than Pact.

**Mana.** The deck has 20 lands, and `check_deck` found no issues. The simulation of 5,000 games gave:
- Mulligan rate was 8.6%, against 8.5% for the reference Song list.
- Colour problems were 7% on turn 1 and about 5% by turn 4 (93% and 94.9% colour-OK).
- The "screw rate" was 25%, the same as the reference list.
- `draw_odds` gives a 56.6% chance of seeing at least one of the 4 Song of Creation by turn 5 on the play.
- It gives a 46.2% chance of seeing at least one of the 3 Oracle or Jace cards by turn 5 on the play.
- It gives a 25% chance of seeing both by turn 5.
- The simulator does not model card abilities, so it can't tell you how often the combo actually wins. I have no measured win rate.

**Sideboard.** It is the borrowed list with one small change: I moved Tormod's Crypt out of the main deck.
- **Against graveyard decks** (Goryo's Vengeance, Living End, Dredge): bring in Tormod's Crypt, Nature's Claim and Pithing Needle.
- **Against artifact decks** (Affinity, Eldrazi Tron): bring in Haywire Mite and Nature's Claim.
- **Against creature decks:** bring in Unholy Heat and Fire Magic.
- **Against fast combo and control:** bring in Consign to Memory and Pact of Negation, and use Swan Song and Veil of Summer to protect Song of Creation.

**Label: brew.** I took the 5-0 Song of Creation list from a Modern League on 2026-09-28 and changed it: −1 Tormod's Crypt, −1 Preordain, +2 Thassa's Oracle. I haven't tested these swaps in play. Whether Oracle beats the other cards it replaces is my judgment. Fewer Crypt and Preordain is a small cost, but it is a cost.

intent.goal: A functional Modern deck built around the Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact combination, with a coherent plan to assemble and win with it.

facts: Thassa's Oracle is legal in modern.
Tainted Pact is not legal in modern.
